subject: Mistral Commerce - sudden latency & 5xx spike (VPC peering path)
messages:
From: Susan Wei <susan.wei@mistralcommerce.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: support@mistralcommerce.com, Carlos Vega <c.vega@mistralcommerce.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: High latency and 500s for inference requests — urgent

Ben —

We started seeing a huge spike in latency (~1.2s to 6s p95) and intermittent 5xx errors across our checkout inference path at ~09:00 PDT. This is impacting live transactions and causing failed recommendations. The surge aligns with several large holds we have in production right now; traffic is not unusually high from our side.

Attached are a short trace bundle and a couple of sample 500 logs. Can you confirm if anything changed on your side (routing, peering, or proxy policies)? This needs executive visibility — our VP of Engineering wants an update in 30 minutes.

—Susan
VP, Platform — Mistral Commerce

Attachments: mistral_trace-20280402.zip (traces), mistral_500-sample.log (sample 500 responses)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Susan — thanks for the traces and the heads up. We're on it. I've looped in network + infra (Jonas) and the on-call SRE (Evelyn). Jonas — can you confirm whether the peering route flapped or if any firewall/proxy rules changed?

We'll escalate to the incident bridge and get an exec brief to your VP within 30 mins.

Action items:
- Jonas to validate peering state and NAT/firewall counters
- Evelyn to correlate Redwood token-level errors and retries with Mistral traces
- I'll handle customer comms and exec sync (looping Marissa for credits/contract sensitivity)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 09:41:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency and 500s for inference requests — urgent

Ben / team — quick update from the infra side:
- Peering BGP session to Mistral's edge (prefix 198.51.100.0/22) experienced intermittent route withdraws between 08:58 and 09:10 PDT; observed route flaps on two transit hops outside our immediate fabric.
- Concurrently saw a spike in DNS resolution latencies from our proxy tier for Mistral's gateway hostnames; cache miss rate jumped ~18% which increased upstream queries.
- Firewall counters show increased SYN retries hitting a single NAT pool — looks like asymmetric pathing caused many connections to be re-mapped mid-flow leading to retransmits and 502s.

Immediate mitigations applied at 09:30:
1) Temporarily moved Mistral's traffic onto alternate peering path (route preference adjusted to avoid the flapping transit).
2) Increased DNS cache TTLs for Mistral hostnames and primed caches on the proxy fleet.
3) Rebalanced NAT allocations for the session pools touching Mistral endpoints.

Preliminary result: p95 latency dropped from ~6s to ~1.1s for a subset of requests; 5xx rate reduced but not fully resolved (still ~0.6% vs baseline 0.02%). I'm keeping the failover in place while we validate stability.

Jonas Weber
Network Infra Lead — Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Susan Wei <susan.wei@mistralcommerce.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 10:03:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency and 500s for inference requests — urgent

Susan / Ben —
On correlating Redwood token traces with the samples you sent, the 5xx responses line up with proxy 502/504s and a small number of TLS handshake timeouts. The traces show retries that inflate apparent latency (client-side retries + server queueing).

Next steps we recommend:
- Keep the alternate peering path for 1 hour while we monitor.
- We'll open a transit provider ticket for the mid-hop flaps; that will take longer to remediate.
- As a short-term application-level mitigation, we can enable extra retry suppression for Mistral's route (reduce client retries and increase circuit-breaker thresholds) — that'll lower downstream pressure and reduce token duplication.

I've attached an observation log to the incident JIRA with timing and sample IDs. Will monitor closely and update in 30 min.

Evelyn Hart
On-call SRE — Redwood Inference
Attachment: mistral_500-sample.log
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Susan Wei <susan.wei@mistralcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2028 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency and 500s for inference requests — urgent

Susan — following up with an exec summary and next steps after 24h of observation.

Summary:
- Root cause: transient peering route instability in a third-party transit provider caused asymmetric paths. That, combined with DNS cache churn and NAT pool imbalance on our proxy tier, produced spikes in latency and a higher 5xx rate.
- Mitigations performed: temporary peering failover, DNS cache priming, NAT rebalancing, and application-level retry suppression. Results: p95 returns near baseline for most flows; 5xx rate dropped to 0.05% (still slightly elevated).
- Longer-term actions: permanent multi-path peering for Mistral prefixes, hardened BGP resilience with transit provider, and a proxy NAT redesign to avoid single-pool hotspots. Estimated timeline: 2–3 weeks for peering & NAT changes; transit provider RCA TBD.

Ask of Mistral: please confirm whether Mistral can temporarily spread a small portion of traffic to a secondary region (us-west-1) while we finalize permanent peering changes. This would reduce risk during the transit provider rollout window.

Marissa — I've noted credit sensitivity for the account; can you open an approvals thread for a goodwill credit if our final SLA numbers fall short for April?

Ben Carter
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference
